title: Michael Burry says he 'tried to warn' investors that Nvidia, CoreWeave, and Nebius were headed for trouble
excerpt: Michael Burry of "The Big Short" fame said he tried to warn investors a selloff was coming, and he sees deeper issues than Jensen Huang and politics.
content_html:
By Theron Mohamed

You're currently following this author! Click to unsubscribe from email alerts.

2026-11-20T14:59:09.049Z

Michael Burry has a message for everyone who bet on AI infrastructure stocks and lost money: I told you so.

"CoreWeave, Nebius, Nvidia, semis, I tried to warn you all," Burry said in an X post on Thursday. "I didn't say short. But I provided the information one would need to sell."

Coreweave, Nebius, NVIDIA, semis, I tried to warn you all. I didn’t say short. But I provided the information one would need to sell.

— Cassandra Unchained (@michaeljburry) November 19, 2026

Nvidia shares opened about 4% lower on Friday, while CoreWeave and Nebius fell around 7%.

The trio are down about 42%, 55%, and 65% respectively from their intraday highs on October 6, the day before the current AI drawdown began. The NYSE Semiconductor Index has slumped by about 30% over the same period.

On November 11, the day before Jensen Huang resigned as Nvidia's CEO, Burry urged shareholders in a Substack post to "get out" of the AI chipmaker's stock. He predicted it would grow more slowly and its profit margins would shrink without the prolific dealmaker in charge.

Burry cautioned that Nvidia partners such as Nebius and CoreWeave — so-called "neoclouds" that build data centers and rent access to Nvidia chips and other AI infrastructure — could be caught in the fallout in a November 12 post.

He said they've "benefited greatly from Nvidia's market power and largesse, which seems to have entered a new paradigm now."

Burry declared on August 12 that "Nebius is what the top of a boom looks like." The stock closed at $259 that day, 62% higher than its November 19 close.

A week earlier, on August 6, Burry said he couldn't resist shorting Nebius and Oracle, saying it was a "bit like shooting fish in a barrel." He's also shorted Nvidia, CoreWeave, and chip indexes this year.

Burry has been loudly skeptical of the stratospheric rise in AI stocks since he pivoted from running a hedge fund to writing a Substack about his personal investments a year ago.

The contrarian investor, one of the few people to predict and profit from the collapse of the mid-2000s housing bubble, has warned AI companies are overinvesting in fast-depreciating assets such as microchips and data centers.

He's also called out their aggressive accounting, circular-financing deals, and dangerous levels of debt and off-balance-sheet liabilities.

Burry emphasized in a late Thursday post on X that he has far deeper concerns about Nvidia and its partners and peers than Huang's alleged extramarital affairs, and a potentially less AI-friendly environment with Democrats in charge of the House and Senate.

"If you think this is still all about an affair and some politics, you're not thinking hard enough," he wrote.

If you think this is still all about an affair and some politics, you're not thinking hard enough.

— Cassandra Unchained (@michaeljburry) November 20, 2026
